about: Official guidelines (targets) and international benchmarks for the indicators of CityPulse V2. 'references' holds only what a skeptic opened and confirmed (value, year, fit); 'rejected' holds what failed that check and is never used; 'none' lists the indicators with no verified reference and where it was looked. The product reads src/catalog/indicators.js (guideline, benchmark), written from this file.

fields.role: guideline = the official target of the indicator; benchmark = an international figure shown as context
fields.judges: true only when the target measures the same thing in the same unit, so the status may use it
fields.direction: atLeast = the figure should reach the value or more; atMost = the figure should stay at the value or less
fields.unit: the catalogue unit token of the indicator when comparable; pct_reduction = a national relative cut (not comparable)

references.title: Goal 3: Ensure healthy lives and promote well-being for all at all ages
references.caveat: Different age band: under five, not under one. Deaths before age one are part of it, so it works only as a very loose upper limit, not as a standard. A global aspiration for countries, not for a city; Israel is far below it.
references.verifierNote: sdgs.un.org/goals/goal3 opened: target 3.2 reads 'by 2030 end preventable deaths of newborns and children under 5', neonatal 'at least as low as 12' and under-5 'at least as low as 25 per 1,000 live births'.

references.publisher: Ministry of Transport and Road Safety (National Road Safety Authority)
references.title: פעולות עיקריות לתכנית לאומית לבטיחות בדרכים לשנים 2026-2030
references.caveat: Five-year goal: cut severe harm by 25% against the average of 2020-2024; deaths in 2030 not above 273. Counts people, national only, relative reduction, not a rate per 100,000 and not per town; 'severe harm' is not defined on the page. Cover reads July 2024, updated February 2025 and August 2025 (year taken as 2025). Government approval reported by Calcalist (16 Nov 2025); the decision text was not found. National context only, never a bar for a town's rate.
references.verifierNote: Downloaded the PDF and viewed page 5 (section 'יעדי התכנית'): reduction of severe harm by 25% over five years versus the 2020-2024 average, deaths in 2030 not above 273, top-ten safest countries; cover shows July 2024 with updates Feb 2025 and Aug 2025; Calcalist article dated 16.11.25 confirms government approval.

references.yearNote: 2021 or the latest year available per country (some countries 2017-2023)
references.title: OECD Family Database, CO2.2 Child poverty
references.caveat: OECD country average, not a target; the indicator is descriptive (no good or bad direction), so context only. OECD poverty is on equivalised household disposable income with a square-root scale and ages 0-17; the National Insurance Institute counts children in poor families on net income per standard person, so the local figure is not like-for-like. The page says Israel is among six countries above 20 percent.
references.verifierNote: Extracted the PDF text (updated November 2024): 'On average across OECD countries, 12.2% of children live in relative income poverty', threshold 50% of median disposable income, data 2021 or latest, Israel listed among six countries with more than 20 percent.
